v1.feedback: The audio-amplifier parent DNA survives clearly (mic reactivity, bass shockwave, chromatic aberration on impact) and the psaltery word genuinely drives the morph target — trapezoidal frame with vibrating strings resonating on bass is a smart conceptual bridge. Two issues to fix: the morph is a one-way 50-second creep, so the first half of viewing is just the unmodified cypress parent — consider starting morph at 0.3+ or making it oscillate so the psaltery influence is visible within 2 seconds of load. Second, the psaltery silhouette (trapezoid + vertical lines) lacks the instant readability of the cypress tree it replaces — thicken the frame particles and add slight curvature to the string endpoints so the instrument shape reads as a physical object rather than a geometric wireframe.

v2.feedback: The psaltery target shape is well-constructed — trapezoidal frame, catenary strings, soundhole, bridge are all legible and show the word drove the design. The L-system cypress parent carries over nicely as a vertical branching form, and bass-driven string vibration is a smart audio_amplifier lineage marker. Two concerns: during the mid-morph transition (~30-60%) the interpolated positions will likely produce an ambiguous blob between tree and instrument — consider snapping branches onto string lines rather than linear lerp so the form stays readable throughout. Also at 30K particles split across frame+strings+tree, the strings may read thin on high-DPI displays; biasing more particles toward the string catenary curves would sharpen the psaltery silhouette when it dominates.
